name: render-path-budget
description: Limits per landing surface for a first-time mobile visitor who doesn't scroll, checked by ./bench.sh budget (Lighthouse on the generator, median of the runs). A limit is a measured value plus a margin, so the budget passes today and fails on a regression. Byte limits are in bytes. targets holds what counts as good and never fails a run. cpu_slowdown is Lighthouse's CPU slowdown that the LCP, TBT, and score limits are calibrated for: a run with another one fails those lines. See docs/benchmarks/viral-spike-render-path-budget.md.

home.note: The start page (docs/implementation/start-page-redesign.md): a search over the painted room, Where to start below. Recalibrated 2026-10-29 from a local production build behind TLS and HTTP/2 with 103 hints (CPU-capped mobile Lighthouse, 9 runs each, the old TV page measured the same way): images 17 -> 59 and image bytes 94 KB -> 853 KB (the shelf covers, the card's fan and the browse rails' posters, all after the room), total bytes 688 KB -> 1.24 MB, render-blocking 5 -> 6 (five page sheets), while scripts went 42 -> 34 and script bytes 534 -> 341 KB and HTML stays 29 KB; those caps are unchanged. LCP and score caps are unchanged until a generator run calibrates them.
